evidence_method: read-only public primary documentation plus project-maintainer issue/release history; no downloaded code or product was executed

sources.title: MQTT Version 5.0
sources.released_version_or_commit: OASIS Standard, MQTT Version 5.0, 2019-03-07 (versioned authoritative HTML; latest v5.0 URI is linked from document)
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of the public, versioned OASIS standard; inspected the cited sections. No MQTT client, broker, radio or device was operated.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: QoS 0 allows loss; QoS 1 is at least once and allows duplicates; QoS 2 is protocol-level exactly-once with extra exchanges. Packet identifiers are reusable after PUBACK; DUP flags a PUBLISH packet, not necessarily a repeated observation, and a repeated application message can arrive with DUP=0/new packet ID. MQTT 5 absent Session Expiry Interval means 0, ending session on disconnect; a positive interval requires storing state, but documented storage has implementation/admin/failure limits. MQTT requires an ordered lossless underlying stream; spec does not specify radio/gateway behavior.
sources.applicability: Normative MQTT v5 protocol semantics only. Conditional on actual station/gateway using MQTT v5; does not establish which protocol or hardware the club uses or guarantee sensor sampling/archive behavior.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: low-bandwidth/constrained M2M/IoT rationale and small overhead are explicit; QoS and session claims/limits as summarized above.

sources.title: Telegraf MQTT Consumer Input Plugin
sources.released_version_or_commit: Telegraf v1 documentation (rolling, exact binary/release not pinned); page says plugin introduced in v0.10.3.
sources.locator: Plugin overview/tracking metric support and Configuration: QoS, reconnection, max undelivered messages, persistent_session/client_id: web lines 65-83, 120-167.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of official Telegraf plugin documentation/configuration; no plugin or broker was installed or run.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Plugin consumes MQTT broker topics. Tracking metrics can delay source acknowledgment until all outputs receive metrics. Docs show qos default 0 and persistent_session false; for offline messages use persistent session plus stable client_id and QoS 1/2 on both publish and subscribe sides. Documented default MQTT reconnect ceiling is 10 minutes; max undelivered buffer must be tuned relative to batch size.
sources.applicability: Potential gateway-to-ingestion adapter if the club's broker/payload format is compatible. The rolling v1 docs do not pin a release or prove the station payload/output/archive semantics.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: an existing adapter can bridge MQTT directly and has an acknowledgment-after-output-tracking option; this is a useful alternative to custom broker ingestion, conditional on version/configuration review.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 COPY
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 versioned documentation; server minor release not selected.
sources.locator: §COPY Description; ON_ERROR parameter; CSV Format and Notes; psql \copy note. Web lines 49-54, 145-152, 187-204, 238-251.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of PostgreSQL 18 manual; no database command was executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: COPY FROM appends supplied rows. Conversion errors default to stop; `ignore` discards rows and may be unlimited without REJECT_LIMIT. CSV supports quoted embedded CR/LF, but CSV has no universal null/empty convention and quoted whitespace is significant. Server-side COPY file access requires a server-readable path/privilege; psql \copy reads a client-side file via STDIN/STDOUT. COPY invokes triggers/constraints but not rules.
sources.applicability: Candidate staging/import mechanism for a PostgreSQL 18 pilot; exact selected server/client version and CSV producers are unknown, so behavior should be checked there.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: staging COPY can efficiently append a batch, while defaults and CSV edge cases argue for explicit staging, row outcome review and preserving the original file.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 Constraints
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 versioned documentation; server minor release not selected.
sources.locator: §5.5.3 Unique Constraints / NULL treatment: web lines 156-213.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of PostgreSQL 18 manual, including compound uniqueness and NULL behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A unique constraint applies to the listed column/group key. Default NULLS DISTINCT means multiple rows with NULL in a constrained column may coexist; NULLS NOT DISTINCT is an explicit alternative. Primary keys are unique and not null.
sources.applicability: Supports a local design for idempotent ingestion only after the device/CSV source provides a validated stable key. Does not establish an observation's identity or correction semantics.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: transport packet IDs or nullable/inferred tuples are unsuitable as a guaranteed durable deduplication key; uniqueness should be scoped to a declared non-null source identity.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 INSERT
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 versioned documentation; server minor release not selected.
sources.locator: ON CONFLICT Clause: web lines 120-128 and 125, conflict outcomes.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of PostgreSQL 18 manual, conflict actions and atomic upsert conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING suppresses insertion on conflict; DO UPDATE changes the conflicting row and guarantees an insert/update outcome under the stated no-independent-error condition. A target/arbiter constraint or index determines conflicts.
sources.applicability: Potential projection/idempotency mechanism only with a selected valid source key. Avoid using it to mutate/delete raw observation evidence; correction lineage is a separate local product choice.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: a database upsert is not neutral replay handling; its explicit conflict target and action encode a product policy.

sources.title: Apache Beam Window JavaDoc
sources.released_version_or_commit: Apache Beam Java SDK 2.70.0 versioned JavaDoc.
sources.locator: Windowing / Triggers overview and `withAllowedLateness` method: web lines 17-46 and 271-277; versioned page also lines 284-289.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of versioned Java API documentation; no Beam pipeline was built or run.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Windowing uses element event timestamps. Default trigger emits when watermark passes window end and on late arrival, according to docs. An explicitly configured allowed-lateness duration controls how long old windows accept elements/state; elements later than the boundary are dropped and state cleaned up. State/trigger/accumulation mode affect output behavior.
sources.applicability: Conceptual analogue for chart/event-time processing and finite late-update horizons only; Beam is not required/recommended for a ten-station pilot, and its late-data dropping must not be copied into the raw archive.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: event-time grouping, watermark trigger, allowed lateness and cleanup are distinct controls; any pilot chart projection needs an explicit late-data policy.

sources.title: Apache Beam issue #36470
sources.released_version_or_commit: Apache Beam issue opened 2025-10-10; reports watermark caching/filtering added in Beam 2.67 as a contributing context; issue later says fixed in 2.69.0 but current issue milestone displays 2.70.0. No implementation commit was identified in the reviewed issue history.
sources.locator: Issue description and activity, especially cause and fix/release references: web lines 128-169, 224-282.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of Apache Beam maintainers' closed issue; no issue comment was authored and no source patch was executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reported specifically for Spanner Change Stream partitions: possible reordering of metadata-table watermark updates; watermark caching/filtering added in 2.67 exacerbated it. Reported failure was a lower watermark hold than computed lower bound and stuck reading. Issue says milestone 2.70.0 while activity/release note state fix in 2.69.0.
sources.applicability: Bounded historical event-time/progress failure example only; it is not evidence of a defect in weather stations, MQTT, PostgreSQL or the club's devices. Source metadata discrepancy and lack of direct fix commit are retained, not resolved by inference.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: asynchronous metadata updates can make a purported monotonic progress watermark regress and stall an ingestion reader.

sources.locator: Release notes, Bugfixes: web lines 129, 150-162, 202-212; exact fix line 208.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of official Apache Beam release tag and notes.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The v2.69.0 release notes list a fix for Spanner Change Stream reading stuck due to a partition watermark moving backward, linked to issue #36470. Release note confirms a released fix, but does not describe patch mechanics.
sources.applicability: Version-bounded released issue/fix evidence for Beam's Spanner connector; use only as an analogy for explicit ordering/progress tests.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: official release evidence says the identified Beam reader stall was addressed by 2.69.0; source-code change itself was not traced.

sources.title: InfluxDB OSS v2 FAQ — duplicate points
sources.released_version_or_commit: InfluxDB OSS v2 rolling documentation (FAQ contains v2.9.x examples; exact build/commit not pinned). This is not evidence for InfluxDB 3.
sources.locator: Writing data > How does InfluxDB handle duplicate points? and Does timestamp precision matter?: web lines 375-392. Related Line Protocol reference is linked from FAQ.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of official InfluxDB OSS v2 FAQ; no InfluxDB instance or write was used.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A point is identified by measurement, tag set and timestamp. Same-key point writes union field sets; new values win field conflicts. Coarse timestamp precision can collide distinct observations; precision affects write performance.
sources.applicability: Useful alternative for time-series chart projection; documentation behavior is specific to OSS v2 docs and the target release would need confirmation. Not a row-level raw archive or correction-lineage guarantee.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: efficient point storage has collision/merge semantics that may be wrong for distinct same-time readings or corrections unless raw events are separately preserved and point keys are deliberately designed.

sources.title: The Things Stack MQTT Server
sources.released_version_or_commit: The Things Stack documentation landing identifies v3.36.2 at access; this individual docs URL is rolling and not versioned. Deployment type also affects tenant IDs/topics.
sources.locator: MQTT Server overview and note; Subscribing to Upstream Traffic example: page lines 19-34, 57-80, 107-157.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of official The Things Stack integration documentation; no account/key, service, MQTT client or uplink was used.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The Things Stack's MQTT server supports MQTT 3.1.1 and QoS 0 only. It publishes application uplink events on topics, and example payload contains device/gateway metadata. Hosted deployments include tenant ID in topic/user; Open Source does not.
sources.applicability: Conditional on the club actually using LoRaWAN and a compatible The Things Stack deployment/version. QoS 0 is lossy; this server cannot be treated as a QoS1/2 durable application queue. Payload and deployment behavior must be checked for the actual product edition.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: TTS is a plausible LoRaWAN network-server lead but its MQTT integration is QoS 0 only; application archival must be handled elsewhere and gaps/replays must be evaluated.

sources.title: The Things Stack Troubleshooting Console
sources.released_version_or_commit: The Things Stack documentation landing identifies v3.36.2 at access; individual page is rolling/unversioned.
sources.locator: Common Errors > Entity Not Found / Device Not Found and Duplicate Uplink: page lines 46-56.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of official The Things Stack Console troubleshooting page; no live device/gateway was inspected.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: TTS docs say an ABP device reset of frame counters (commonly power cycle) can fail matching the session; OTAA avoids this particular case. A duplicate uplink is an uplink heard by multiple gateways where a late copy arrives outside the deduplication window and is dropped.
sources.applicability: LoRaWAN/TTS-specific network behavior only. Its deduplication is multiple-gateway reception handling, not general application replay/correction policy.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: a network server's dedup window can remove a late radio copy without identifying or correcting an application-level weather observation.

sources.title: The Things Stack Device Best Practices
sources.released_version_or_commit: The Things Stack documentation landing identifies v3.36.2 at access; individual page is rolling/unversioned.
sources.locator: Limit Transmission Length/Payload Size/Duty Cycle; Expect Packet Loss; Power Cycles; Frame Counters: page lines 35-48 and 82-92.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of official device best-practices page; no hardware settings were changed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: For LoRaWAN devices in this product context, docs recommend minimizing transmission length/frequency, avoiding confirmed uplinks unless assurance is necessary, and expecting packet loss (docs say up to 10%). Devices should save session parameters, including FCnt, across normal power cycles; frame counters increment per uplink/downlink and 32-bit counters are recommended.
sources.applicability: Only if actual stations use LoRaWAN; not a blanket standard assertion for other radios. Does not establish the club devices' firmware, local storage or clock quality.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: low-power design trades airtime/reliability, and counter continuity depends on device persistence; the steward must identify the actual protocol and reset behavior.

sources.title: The Things Stack Storage Integration
sources.released_version_or_commit: The Things Stack documentation landing identifies v3.36.2 at access; individual page is rolling/unversioned. Storage retention differs by Cloud, Sandbox and Enterprise deployment.
sources.locator: How it works, retention and batch delay, message download/retrieval: page lines 17-35, 50-70, 79-83.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of official TTS Storage Integration docs; no data was written or retrieved from a service.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Configured upstream messages and relevant metadata are written to a persistent database. Retention is 30 days on Cloud, 24 hours on Sandbox, configurable on Enterprise; Cloud stores only uplinks. Writes occur in batches and may be delayed, and the docs say not to use it for realtime querying.
sources.applicability: Potential bounded buffer/retrieval aid under a chosen deployment, not the club's long-term archive or a freshness source without edition and latency validation.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: TTS has a storage integration worth evaluating, but its version/edition-specific retention is shorter/configurable and its write timing is delayed.

sources.title: The Things Stack issue #4502: ABP frame counter reset behaviour
sources.released_version_or_commit: Maintainer repository issue opened 2021-08-08; reporter environment The Things Stack 3.14.0; closed as completed 2021-09-22. No release tag/implementation commit is linked in the reviewed issue, so this is not treated as a released fix chain.
sources.locator: Issue summary/environment; maintainer comments on duplicate FCnt/cooldown; closure: page lines 129-181, 198-229, 243-259, 276-301, 326-350.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval of The Things Stack open-source maintainer issue/history; no test device or source code was run.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reported ABP reboot with frame counter reset to 0 can have the repeated fcnt=0 treated as duplicate. Maintainer describes existing same-FCnt duplicate handling: default 200ms multi-gateway/peering deduplication window and 1s cooldown dropping duplicates, with later copies processed as retransmissions subject to protocol limits. Maintainer closed the proposed FCnt=0 exception as completed after explaining why behavior is intentional; no code fix/release is evidenced here.
sources.applicability: Useful TTS/LoRaWAN-specific case showing that network replay policy can discard a reset-counter frame and delayed duplicates; not a generic radio rule or approved behavior for this club. Distinct from the Beam released-fix chain in S07-S08.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: receiver duplicate policy relies on protocol identity and bounded windows; repeated counter after reboot may be indistinguishable from replay under that protocol.

sources.title: The Things Stack Data Formats
sources.released_version_or_commit: The Things Stack documentation landing identifies v3.36.2 at access; individual page is rolling/unversioned. The page notes uplink device attributes support was added in v3.34.0.
sources.locator: Data Formats > uplink message JSON examples (`received_at`, nested `uplink_message.received_at`, `f_cnt`); primary page retrieval exposed zero text lines, but the official search extract showed these fields. Treat locator as heading-level and bounded evidence only.
sources.observed_operation: Read-only retrieval/extract of the official data-format page; direct page parser exposed no lines, so exact field context remains to verify against the chosen v3.36.2 deployment.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Search extract defines outer `received_at` as Application Server receipt time and nested uplink `received_at` as Network Server receipt time; data format examples include `f_cnt`. Empty fields may be omitted per doc note.
sources.applicability: Could distinguish server receipt layers and LoRaWAN frame counters in TTS events; does not establish a station sensor's observation time, and field presence/version must be verified for the actual deployment.
sources.bounded_evidence: Paraphrase: TTS event formats expose receipt metadata, which is distinct from station observation time.
